LESSON: MAKING TACKING STITCHES

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: PRODUCTION TECHNIQUES Strand Sub strand Specific learning outcomes Suggested lea
Topic 4.1: Making Tacking Stitches

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Making Tacking Stitches. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we use tacking stitches in making items?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the types of tacking stitches in sewing

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MAKING TACKING STITCHES
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Making Tacking Stitches helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: MAKING TACKING STITCHES
Study Making Tacking Stitches like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the types of tacking stitches in sewing

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the types of tacking stitches in sewing. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the types of tacking stitches in sewing.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Making Tacking Stitches” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the types of tacking stitches in sewing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Making Tacking Stitches is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Making Tacking Stitches” around your school. (skill: identify the types of tacking stitches in sewing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Making Tacking Stitches to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the types of tacking stitches in sewing.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Making Tacking Stitches from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Making Tacking Stitches: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Making Tacking Stitches?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we use tacking stitches in making items?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Making Tacking Stitches means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the types of tacking stitches in sewing.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
